title: How to hedge SPY Without Destroying your Profits
text: The way to think about long puts, especially with respect to hedging a portfolio, is you kind of have to pick them up before you think they you need them, but carrying them perpetually is just not the move. So, that's the first thing you could do is think of the scenarios that you would really want that protection, and then focus on gaining exposure around those periods, but just effectively saying I never want to lose more than 10% of my portfolio is just too expensive. You're not going to walk away with anything. You're paid to take risk. The other thing you can do is actually use scaling in and out instead. So, if the market starts going down or slowing down at the point where you would want to buy protection, just decrease your position size, lock in some of your profit, and then decrease your total exposure. And then you'll say, "Well, what if it goes back up?" If it goes back up, you can buy again, but you're not carrying that put hedge that again is always eroding your P&L.
